problem: Given that $m\ge 1$ is an integer, simplify $\frac{(2m)!\,(m+4)!}{(m+5)!\,(2m-1)!}.$
worked_solution:
First, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}(m+5)! & =(m+5)(m+4)! \\ 2m! & =2m(2m-1)!\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we can cancel the $(m+4)!$ and $(2m-1)!$ that occur in both the numerator and the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(2m)!\,(m+4)!}{(m+5)!\,(2m-1)!} & =\frac{(2m)\,\cdot (2m-1)!\cdot (m+4)!}{(m+5)\cdot (m+4)!\cdot (2m-1)!} \\  & =\frac{(2m)\,\cdot \cancel{(2m-1)!}\cdot \cancel{(m+4)!}}{(m+5)\cdot \cancel{(m+4)!}\cdot \cancel{(2m-1)!}} \\  & =\frac{2m}{m+5}\end{aligned}
$$
